The instant appeal has been filed challenging the finding on liability.

2. The first respondent filed a claim petition stating that on 26.05.2003, while he was driving his car, a tanker lorry insured with the appellant came in the opposite direction and dashed against the National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Vellimuthu on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28817193/
1 car, causing grievous injuries to him.

sentences.text: 3. The second respondent/owner of the lorry remained ex parte before the Tribunal.

4. The appellant filed a counter stating that the accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of the insured vehicle; that in any case, the driver of the insured vehicle did not have a valid licence to drive a heavy motor vehicle carrying inflammable substance; and that at the time of accident, the insured vehicle was transporting a highly inflammable substance and hence, they are not liable to pay compensation.
_______ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
Before the Tribunal, the first respondent examined himself as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and marked Exs.P1 to P12.

The appellant examined R.W.1 to R.W.2 and marked Exs.R1 to R4.
6.

The Tribunal, after taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence, had directed the appellant to pay the compensation at Rs.1,63,750/-.
7.

The learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submitted that though they had challenged the quantum of compensation while filing the appeal, he would be unable to point out any infirmity in the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal; that the Tribunal ought to have held that the appellant is not liable to pay compensation, since the driver of the vehicle did not have a valid licence to drive the tanker lorry carrying inflammable substances; and that in any case,
the Tribunal ought to have given liberty to pay and recover the compensation from the owner.
8. Though notice sent to the respondents has been served, none has entered appearance.
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.
The only point for consideration in the instant appeal is whether the appellant is liable to pay compensation?

10. The appellant had examined R.W.2-Baskaran, who was a Junior Engineer working in the RTO,
Trichy.

He had deposed that the driver of the insured vehicle, one Thangavel had obtained a licence from their office for driving light motor vehicles and heavy motor vehicles, besides the licence to drive a tanker lorry to carry inflammable substances.
However, R.W.2 had deposed that the said licence was obtained on 26.03.2001 and the licence is liable to be renewed every year.

He had,
further, deposed that the said driver had not applied for renewal of licence in their office and even if he had applied for renewal in any other RTO office, he has to first obtain No Objection Certificate from their office; and that their office had not issued any No Objection Certificate.

11. In the light of the said evidence, it is clear that the appellant had established that the driver of the insured vehicle did not have a valid licence to drive a heavy motor vehicle carrying inflammable substances.

12. The owner of the lorry had chosen to remain ex parte before the Tribunal and also before this Court.

13. Since the appellant has established that there was a violation of the policy conditions inasmuch as the driver did not have a valid licence, the appellant would be liable to pay the compensation at the first instance and thereafter, recover it from the owner/second respondent herein.

14. Hence, the appellant/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation at Rs.1,63,750/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty only) with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization (excluding the period of dismissal for default if any) and proportionate costs, less the amount already deposited, if any,
within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

15. On such deposit, the first respondent/claimant is permitted to withdraw the award amount with interest and costs, less the amount already withdrawn, if any, by filing appropriate application before the Tribunal.
__ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 16.
It is open to the appellant to recover the compensation from the second respondent/owner of the vehicle in the manner known to law.
17. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.

Consequently,
connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
